column1: # Vieuville-Nevers Cipher (1589), reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo, printed as a clean digital table
# ("Cipher between Marquis of Vieuville and Duke of Nevers (1589)") in sources/cryptiana/web/nevers.htm,
# section id=BnFfr3641, image phelippes8.png (fetched from cryptiana.web.fc2.com/code/phelippes8.png,
# INTAKE-4715, 27 Sept 2026; sources/cryptiana/web/img/phelippes8.png). Homophonic substitution: letter ->
# one or more numeric code groups (no reconstructed values for j, k, v, w -- French cipher convention, i
# covers j, u covers v; column b carries only one value; column z carries none). "sign" is the printed code
# number (decode direction: sign -> plaintext letter); "value" is the plaintext letter. This is a printed
# digital table, not a hand-drawn manuscript key, so read by direct inspection plus one independent blind
# Sonnet subagent read (general-purpose agent, shown only the image, no context) as a cross-check, per this
# job's brief; the two disagreed on whether "64" sits under column h or column i, settled by this worker
# pixel-cropping and zooming that region of the image directly (3x resize, LANCZOS) -- "64" is under i, not
# h (crop /tmp/crop_fi.png this session, not committed). All plain numeric cells: grade AB (both reads
# agreed, and/or settled by a zoomed crop against unambiguous printed digits). Two cells carry a non-numeric
# printed glyph instead of a digit, transcribed as drawn per CLAUDE.md Usage-adjacent CRYPT B4 convention
# (marks recorded separately, not folded into a digit guess): grade M, meaning uncertain.
# nevers.htm's own prose adds a caveat this table does not capture: "Figures with a dot over the first digit
# are code numbers representing common words" (a separate word-code layer, illustrated only for a sibling
# letter in BnF fr.3633 f.22, not enumerated here) -- a decode pass against this key should not assume every
# digit group decodes as a single dotless letter-homophone; an unmatched or oddly-placed group may be one of
# these undocumented word-codes instead of a transcription error.
sign
